title: Active members
prompt: Return the names of active members, alphabetically. Active means active = 1. Output one name per row.
schema: CREATE TABLE members (id INTEGER, name TEXT, active INTEGER);
starter:
SELECT name
FROM members
WHERE ...
ORDER BY name;
solution: SELECT name FROM members WHERE active = 1 ORDER BY name;

title: Top three products
prompt: Return product names and prices for the three most expensive products. Break price ties by name alphabetically.
schema: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER, name TEXT, price INTEGER);
starter:
SELECT name, price
FROM products
ORDER BY ...
LIMIT 3;
solution: SELECT name, price FROM products ORDER BY price DESC, name ASC LIMIT 3;

title: Missing city data
prompt: Return customer IDs whose city is unknown (NULL), in ascending ID order. An empty string is a known value for this exercise.
schema: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER, city TEXT);
starter:
SELECT id
FROM customers
WHERE ...
ORDER BY id;
solution: SELECT id FROM customers WHERE city IS NULL ORDER BY id;

title: Orders per customer
prompt: Return every customer ID, name, and number of orders, including customers with zero orders. Order by customer ID.
schema: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER, name TEXT); CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER, customer_id INTEGER);
starter:
SELECT c.id, c.name, COUNT(...)
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON ...
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
ORDER BY c.id;
solution: SELECT c.id, c.name, COUNT(o.id) FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name ORDER BY c.id;

cases.seed: INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'Ada'),(2,'Mira'),(3,'Ben'); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11,1),(12,1),(13,3);
INSERT INTO customers VALUES (4,'Kai'),(5,'Lia'); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (20,5),(21,5),(22,5);

title: Revenue by category
prompt: Return each category name and total revenue, where revenue is quantity times unit price. Include categories with no sales as zero. Order by category name.
schema: CREATE TABLE categories (id INTEGER, name TEXT); CREATE TABLE sales (id INTEGER, category_id INTEGER, quantity INTEGER, unit_price INTEGER);
starter:
SELECT c.name, COALESCE(SUM(...), 0)
FROM categories c
LEFT JOIN sales s ON ...
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
ORDER BY c.name;
solution: SELECT c.name, COALESCE(SUM(s.quantity * s.unit_price), 0) FROM categories c LEFT JOIN sales s ON s.category_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name ORDER BY c.name;

cases.seed: INSERT INTO categories VALUES (1,'Books'),(2,'Games'),(3,'Music'); INSERT INTO sales VALUES (1,1,2,10),(2,1,1,12),(3,2,3,7);
INSERT INTO categories VALUES (8,'Tools'),(9,'Art'); INSERT INTO sales VALUES (4,9,5,4),(5,9,2,9);

title: Repeat buyers
prompt: Return customer IDs and their order counts for customers with at least two orders. Sort by count descending, then customer ID ascending.
schema: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER, customer_id INTEGER);
starter:
SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*)
FROM orders
GROUP BY customer_id
HAVING ...
ORDER BY ...;
solution: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, customer_id ASC;

title: Latest ticket status
prompt: Return each ticket ID and its most recent status. A larger event ID breaks ties on occurred_at. Order by ticket ID.
schema: CREATE TABLE ticket_events (event_id INTEGER, ticket_id INTEGER, status TEXT, occurred_at TEXT);
solution: WITH ranked AS (SELECT ticket_id, status, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ticket_id ORDER BY occurred_at DESC, event_id DESC) AS rn FROM ticket_events) SELECT ticket_id, status FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY ticket_id;

title: Second distinct salary
prompt: Return the second highest distinct salary as one row, one column. Each fixture has at least two distinct salaries.
schema: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER, salary INTEGER);
starter:
SELECT DISTINCT salary
FROM employees
ORDER BY salary DESC
LIMIT ... OFFSET ...;
solution: SELECT DISTINCT salary FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1;

title: Running account balance
prompt: Return account ID, transaction ID, and running balance for every transaction. Credits are positive and debits negative. Order by account ID, then transaction ID.
schema: CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER, account_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER);
starter:
SELECT account_id, id,
       SUM(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY ...) AS balance
FROM transactions
ORDER BY account_id, id;
solution: SELECT account_id, id, SUM(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS balance FROM transactions ORDER BY account_id, id;

title: Monthly revenue change
prompt: Group sales by calendar month (YYYY-MM). Return month, total revenue, and change from the previous recorded month. For the first month, use its total as the change. Order by month.
schema: CREATE TABLE sales (id INTEGER, sold_at TEXT, amount INTEGER);
solution: WITH months AS (SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', sold_at) AS month, SUM(amount) AS revenue FROM sales GROUP BY 1) SELECT month, revenue, revenue - LAG(revenue, 1, 0) OVER (ORDER BY month) FROM months ORDER BY month;

title: Longest login streak
prompt: Return each user ID and their longest run of consecutive distinct login dates. Order by user ID. A user can have duplicate logins on one date.
schema: CREATE TABLE logins (user_id INTEGER, login_date TEXT);
starter:
WITH days AS (SELECT DISTINCT user_id, login_date FROM logins),
numbered AS (
  SELECT user_id, login_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY login_date) AS rn
  FROM days
)
-- Group by user_id and julianday(login_date) - rn.
SELECT ...;
solution: WITH days AS (SELECT DISTINCT user_id, login_date FROM logins), numbered AS (SELECT user_id, login_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY login_date) AS rn FROM days), runs AS (SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) AS streak FROM numbered GROUP BY user_id, julianday(login_date) - rn) SELECT user_id, MAX(streak) FROM runs GROUP BY user_id ORDER BY user_id;

title: Depth in the team tree
prompt: Return each employee ID and their depth below the root manager. Roots have manager_id NULL and depth 0. Order by employee ID.
schema: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER, manager_id INTEGER);
solution: WITH RECURSIVE tree(id, depth) AS (SELECT id, 0 FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT e.id, tree.depth + 1 FROM employees e JOIN tree ON e.manager_id = tree.id) SELECT id, depth FROM tree ORDER BY id;
